extracted.intended_audience: elementary literacy teachers, instructional coaches, and literacy researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for implementing and scoring a 6+1 Traits-of-Writing rubric (adapted for grades 3–4) as both an instructional tool and assessment for elementary students.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6+1 TRAIT model (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 6+1 TRAIT model summarized the writing traits as ideas, organization, voice, word choice, sentence fluency, conventions, and presentation (+1). The framework can be used to teach students to identify the traits of good writing, self-evaluate their writing, and set goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model includes instructional strategies and involves the use of rubrics for scoring students' writing. The researcher introduced the traits framework for instruction and assessment and developed teacher and student versions of rubrics based on the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas refer to the author's message and the content. (Appendix C descriptors: Shows understanding of the writing task/genre. Has a clear central idea. All details/examples support the central idea. Uses original ideas.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student 'I can' statements: I can choose an idea or topic; I can write about real people, events or ideas; I can add details about my idea or topic; I can express why this topic/idea is important to me. Used as focus for mini-lessons, mentor texts, and goal-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization is the structure of the writing. (Appendix C descriptors: Expository writing structure, uses transitions to connect sentences/paragraphs, introduction and conclusion support the central idea and genre.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional guidance: mini-lessons target topic sentences, paragraphing, linking to reading, main ideas and supporting details. Student 'I can' statements include writing central idea, supporting sentences, conclusion, and transitions. Mentor texts and anchor charts used to teach organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice reflects the author's feelings and unique style. (Appendix C descriptors: Writing is engaging and thoughtful. Writer's purpose is clear. Expresses writer's unique views and experiences. Tone is appropriate for genre.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student 'I can' statements: I can write how I feel; I can create a tone or mood; I can use my unique words and expressions. Taught via mentor texts and modeled composing to help students develop voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Word choice is defined as vivid and personal language and style. (Appendix C descriptors: Uses interesting words, phrases and language devices; accurate and concise word choice.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student 'I can' statements: I can use parts of speech correctly; I can use interesting words and phrases (figurative language); I can 'paint a picture' with my words. Mini-lessons and mentor texts model powerful word choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence fluency is the smoothness/coherence of sentences. (Appendix C descriptors: Varied sentences, strong sentence-to-sentence connections, supporting sentences with details/explanations.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student 'I can' statements: I can write simple and compound sentences with correct subject-verb agreement; I can start sentences in different ways; I can use different sentence types; I can revise sentences by adding/changing/removing words/phrases. Lessons target complex sentences and fluency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions (including CUPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions are grammar, punctuation, and spelling. The rubric uses 'Mostly correct use of CUPS: Capitalization, Usage (Grammar), Punctuation, Spelling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix C scoring levels: Errors that do not affect meaning vs. inconsistent CUPS limiting meaning vs. persistent errors. Student 'I can' statements list capitalization rules, correct word forms, punctuation, spelling strategies, and use of resources to find correct spellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (+1 trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation addresses the appearance of the writing (the +1 trait).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student 'I can' statements: I can use correct letter formation, spacing, sizes; I can write in cursive; my work is neat; I can use a word processor; I can add text features; I can use a rubric to revise and edit; I can publish my work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score point scale and point allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Score Point system: 4 = Accomplished; 3 = Satisfactory; 2 = Basic; 1 = Limited. The teacher rubric used six traits with a maximum of 24 points (four per criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptors for each score point are provided in Appendix C (per-trait descriptors for 4/3/2/1). Rubric aligned to Grade 4 STAAR scoring language to ensure state-standard alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-friendly 'I can' rubric and self-evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: A student-friendly rubric was developed using all seven trait categories and modified into 'I can' statements based on the third grade TEKS so students could evaluate their writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The student rubric was provided to students before the study and used during conferences to help them set goals and conduct self-evaluations. It is intended to make rubric language accessible for student goal-setting and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric use for instruction and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubrics are used for both instructional planning and assessment: provide the traits focus for mini-lessons, purpose for 'reading like authors', framework for peer and teacher feedback, and an assessment tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers used the rubric when planning lessons, creating a student-friendly version, using writing prompts, and during writing conferences. The model supports using rubrics to guide instruction (mini-lessons), self-assessment, peer collaboration, and monitoring progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with state/district standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptors used in the teacher rubric were based on the Grade 4 Writing Expository Scoring Guide (TEA, 2017) and the district's scoring guide to ensure alignment with state standards for writing instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State requirement cited: it is a state writing standard for students to use rubrics beginning in grade one (TEA, 2008). Alignment informed rubric language and scoring descriptors used in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development and scorer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers received professional development on the 6+1 Traits model and practiced scoring using the rubrics. The researcher modeled lessons, conducted follow-up PD, and teachers practiced scoring student writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD components: explain purpose and descriptors, model use of rubric during workshop and conferences, practice scoring, analyze mentor texts, plan lessons. Fidelity of implementation and teacher understanding were emphasized as central to successful use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mentor/anchor texts and modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentor texts (e.g., River Heart, student and teacher samples, picture books) are used to model traits during minilessons and to support 'reading like writers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor texts selected to teach specific writing traits; anchor text provided to students to refer to repeatedly. Teachers used mentor texts to show examples and composed writing with students that featured targeted traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing workshop structure and instructional practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily writing workshop (approx. one hour) with whole-group minilessons (10–15 minutes), independent writing time, teacher conferences, sharing sessions, and opportunities for frequent writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minilessons focus on one or two traits; teacher models, students apply the trait, conferences provide oral feedback or brief notes; sharing sessions use trait language for peer feedback. Practices drawn from research on effective writing instruction (writing process, frequent writing, peer collaboration, teacher support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring procedures and inter-rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing samples were independently scored by teacher and researcher; inter-rater reliability was measured (Cronbach's Alpha = .82 indicates a high level of agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring procedure used five pre-test and five post-test prompts administered in workshop conditions with prompts read aloud. High inter-rater agreement supports use of one scorer's ratings in analysis; scorer training and double-scoring are implied requirements to ensure reliable rubric application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student goal-setting and conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Students had pre-existing writing goals and developed targets with teacher/researcher during conferences; rubrics were used during conferences to help set goals and for self-evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferences involved identifying a trait the student was using and an area for improvement; feedback was oral or brief written notes. The use of rubrics supported gradual internalization of trait language and self-regulation stages (observation → emulation → self-controlled → self-regulated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment administration conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment administration: prompts read in entirety to students, students had one-hour workshop time to complete essays, same procedures for pre- and post-tests to ensure comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five pre-tests from previous state 4th-grade prompts and five post-tests created by researcher. Prompts and administration procedures standardized to establish baseline and measure effects of intervention.
